Read and write spatial files through GDAL

geo-io.Rd

Tidy readers and writers so you rarely need sf::st_read(), terra::rast(), or raw GDAL utilities. geo_read() auto-detects raster versus vector from the file extension (and GDAL driver when needed). geo_write() picks a writer from the object type and the destination extension. Format-specific twins geo_vector_read() / geo_vector_write() and geo_raster_read() / geo_raster_write() are available when you already know the type. All I/O goes through sf and terra (GDAL / OGR under the hood). Do not use the retired rgdal package.

Supported formats (read unless noted; anything else GDAL reads also works, with type set):

FormatExtensionsTypeNotes
GeoTIFF / COG.tif, .tiffrasterwrite supported
netCDF.nc, .nc4, .cdfrasterclimate and ocean data; pick variables with var, time kept in terra::time()
HDF4 / HDF5.hdf, .h4, .he4, .h5, .hdf5, .he5rasterMODIS, VIIRS, GEDI; pick subdatasets with var
GRIB.grib, .grb, .grib2, .grb2rasterweather model output
Sentinel-2.SAFE folder, .zip, MTD_*.xmlrasterLevel-1C and Level-2A products
JPEG 2000.jp2rasterSentinel-2 band files
ENVI.dat/.bin with .hdr, .envirasterhyperspectral cubes
ERDAS Imagine.imgraster
Zarr.zarrrastercloud-native arrays
Other rasters.asc, .grd, .vrt, .rst, .sdat, .ers, .bil, .bip, .bsqrasterASCII grid, VRT, IDRISI, SAGA, ER Mapper
Band filesseveral pathsrasterstacked into one multi-band raster
GeoPackage.gpkgvector (or raster)preferred vector write
Shapefile.shp (+ sidecars)vectorwrite supported
GeoJSON / TopoJSON.geojson, .json, .topojsonvectorwrite supported
FlatGeobuf.fgbvectorwrite supported
KML / KMZ.kml, .kmzvectorKMZ unzipped to KML
GPS exchange.gpxvectorwaypoints, tracks, routes (layer)
AutoCAD.dxf, .dwgvectorpick CAD layers with cad_layer; DWG needs GDAL's CAD driver
MicroStation.dgnvectorcad_layer filters by level
MapInfo.tab, .mifvector
GML, SQLite / SpatiaLite.gml, .sqlitevector
OpenStreetMap.osm, .pbfvectorlayer = "points", "lines", "multipolygons"
Nautical charts (S-57).000vector
FileGDB.gdbvectorwhen GDAL has OpenFileGDB/FileGDB
Spreadsheets.xlsx, .xls, .odsvectorthrough GDAL; needs lon/lat columns
CSV / text.csv, .tsv, .txtvectorneeds lon/lat columns

Use geo_layers() to see what a file holds (vector layers, netCDF/HDF variables and subdatasets, or AutoCAD layers) before reading it. GADM downloads use these writers for the on-disk cache; see geo_gadm() for license notes (do not redistribute the full GADM database).

Map figures from plot_sites(), plot_geo(), plot_sdm() and plot_topo() are saved with geo_save() (or tidydiversity::plot_save()).

Usage

geo_read(
  path,
  type = NULL,
  driver = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  layer = NULL,
  crs = 4326,
  var = NULL,
  cad_layer = NULL,
  ...
)

geo_vector_read(
  path,
  driver = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  layer = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  cad_layer = NULL,
  ...
)

geo_raster_read(path, driver = NULL, var = NULL, ...)

geo_write(
  x,
  path,
  driver = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  layer = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  crs = 4326,
  ...
)

geo_vector_write(
  data,
  path,
  driver = NULL,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  layer = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  crs = 4326,
  ...
)

geo_raster_write(raster, path, driver = NULL, overwrite = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

path

File path. The extension selects the format unless driver is set.

type

Force "vector" or "raster" in geo_read(); NULL auto-detects.

driver

Optional GDAL/OGR driver name (for example "GPKG", "ESRI Shapefile", "GeoJSON", "GTiff", "netCDF").

lon, lat

Column names used when reading CSV/text or writing a non-sf table. Defaults try lon/lat, then longitude/latitude, then x/y.

layer

Layer name for multi-layer containers (GeoPackage, GDB, GPX, OSM).

crs

CRS assigned to lon/lat tables (default WGS84) and to CAD drawings, which store none (for example 32755 for UTM zone 55S).

var

For netCDF, HDF and GRIB rasters: variable or subdataset names (or numbers) to read, as listed by geo_layers(). NULL reads them all.

cad_layer

For AutoCAD (.dxf, .dwg) and MicroStation (.dgn) files: CAD layers (or DGN levels) to keep. NULL keeps all.

...

Passed to sf::st_read() / sf::st_write() or terra::rast() / terra::writeRaster().

x

Object to write: sf, SpatRaster, or a data frame with lon/lat columns for geo_write() / geo_vector_write().

overwrite

Overwrite an existing file? Default FALSE.

data

Vector object or table for geo_vector_write() (sf or a data frame with lon/lat columns).

raster

A terra::SpatRaster (or coercible) for geo_raster_write().

Value

  • Readers: an sf tibble (tmr_geo_sf) or a terra::SpatRaster.

  • Writers: path, invisibly.

See also

geo_save(), geo_gadm(), as_sf(), as_spat_raster()

Examples

sites <- geo_example_sites("wilhelm")
gpkg <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
geo_write(sites, gpkg, overwrite = TRUE)
geo_read(gpkg)
#> Simple feature collection with 8 features and 6 fields
#> Geometry type: POINT
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 145.058 ymin: -5.81424 xmax: 145.333 ymax: -5.72361
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>     site      lon      lat elevation elevation_band
#> 1 MW0200 145.3330 -5.73561       200          200 m
#> 2 MW0700 145.2535 -5.73258       700          700 m
#> 3 MW1200 145.2690 -5.72361      1200         1200 m
#> 4 MW1700 145.2365 -5.75665      1700         1700 m
#> 5 MW2200 145.1796 -5.76114      2200         2200 m
#> 6 MW2700 145.1529 -5.81424      2700         2700 m
#> 7 MW3200 145.0706 -5.80470      3200         3200 m
#> 8 MW3700 145.0580 -5.78483      3700         3700 m
#>                                  coordinate_note                      geom
#> 1 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946  POINT (145.333 -5.73561)
#> 2 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946 POINT (145.2535 -5.73258)
#> 3 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946  POINT (145.269 -5.72361)
#> 4 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946 POINT (145.2365 -5.75665)
#> 5 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946 POINT (145.1796 -5.76114)
#> 6 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946 POINT (145.1529 -5.81424)

#> 8 published bait GPS, doi:10.5281/zenodo.8191946  POINT (145.058 -5.78483)

r <- terra::rast(
  ncols = 8, nrows = 8, xmin = 144.8, xmax = 145.4,
  ymin = -6, ymax = -5.5, crs = "EPSG:4326"
)
terra::values(r) <- seq_len(terra::ncell(r))
tif <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
geo_raster_write(r, tif, overwrite = TRUE)
geo_raster_read(tif)
